method: Decode actual generated names using the existing $u$/numeric-escape convention. Require the pinned stage-one49.js URL. Select only allocation nodes whose own frame is exactly Map.get.go, Map.lo, or Map.hi.

Traverse every raw heap tree node once, assert unique node IDs, and add each selected node selfSize exactly once. Never sum inclusive subtrees or charge an ancestor a second time. Recursive Map.get.go frames do not duplicate their descendant allocation weights.
Use the ENTIRE raw ancestor chain, not the previous14-frame summary. Find nearest visible non-Map generated compiler frame; inspect Map operation frames between allocation node and that owner.

Definite name-read requires nearest owner exactly checker_arena.name plus a visible Map.get-family frame/current site and no write-family frame. Other get paths are separated. Explicit set/put/ins/del/rem frames identify other writes.

A seek path with nearest owner checker_arena.name.insert is a source-confirmed write (actual49line12121 calls Map.set). Seek paths lacking a visible write marker or that exact source owner remain unresolved; no fabricated read/write ownership.
samples.size weights are separately summed by nodeId. Tree selfSize and sample-size sums are retained independently; neither is an exact allocation counter.

sourceEvidence.meaning: Map.get.go recursively rebuilds a path using Map.lo/hi; its self allocation is distinct from child self allocation.
checker_arena.name evaluates Map.get on name_ids before invoking name.result.
checker_arena.name.insert calls Map.set; name-namespace ancestry alone must not label writes as reads.

boundaries: These are cumulative statistical worker-isolate allocation estimates from one instrumented49 run, not exact bytes/object counts, retained memory, CPU cost, or predicted52 speedup.

Visible stack ownership is conservative: inlined/missing caller frames and opaque closures can leave ownership unresolved. The definite category is supported by recorded frames, not proof that every real name-read allocation was captured or attributed there.
Only the three requested allocation sites are partitioned, not all Map-family allocations, all descendants of a name call, or all Arena reconstruction.

Replacing a read may still allocate in IndexLookup.find/Map.bit/Option handling, and optimization can move allocation attribution. Attributed pre-change bytes are not an asserted removable-byte total.
